title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 16 (Rectification of Name of Company)

content.overview: Section 16 empowers the Central Government to direct a company to change its name if the name is identical with or too nearly resembles an existing company name, or if it was registered by inadvertence or otherwise in a manner that warrants rectification. Non-compliance may lead to the name being changed by the Central Government and penalties.
content.glance: State the Central Government’s power to direct a name change; note resemblance and inadvertent registration grounds; state the consequences of non-compliance.
content.study: If, through inadvertence or otherwise, a company is registered with a name that is identical with or too nearly resembles the name of an existing company, or in other prescribed circumstances, the Central Government may direct the company to change its name within the prescribed period. The company must comply by adopting a new name in accordance with the Act. If it fails to comply, the Central Government may order the name to be changed and the Registrar to enter the new name; the company may also be liable to a fine. The provision protects against confusingly similar names and administrative error in registration. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in s. 16 and link to name rules under s. 4 and name-change procedure under s. 13.

sections.heading: Grounds for Direction
sections.body: Name identical with or too nearly resembling an existing company name, or registration by inadvertence or other prescribed cause.

sections.heading: Central Government Direction
sections.body: The Central Government may direct the company to change its name within the prescribed time.

sections.heading: Company’s Duty to Comply
sections.body: The company must adopt a new compliant name under the Act’s name-change procedure.

sections.heading: Consequences of Non-Compliance
sections.body: Central Government may itself order the name change and Registrar entry; fines may apply.

examples.title: Nearly identical name
examples.body: A new company is registered with a name too nearly resembling an existing listed company’s name. Under s. 16 the Central Government may direct a change.

examples.title: Non-compliance with direction
examples.body: The company ignores the direction to change its name. The Central Government may order the change and the Registrar may enter the new name; penalties may follow.

hypotheticals.question: Is s. 16 limited to names registered by mistake?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It covers identity or close resemblance with existing names as well as inadvertent or other prescribed registration situations.

hypotheticals.question: Can the company choose any new name after a s. 16 direction?
hypotheticals.analysis: The new name must still comply with the Act’s name rules (s. 4 and related provisions) and the name-change procedure under s. 13.

distinctions.title: Rectification (s. 16) vs voluntary name change (s. 13)
distinctions.left: Directed by Central Government for resemblance or error
distinctions.right: Company-initiated change by special resolution and approval

misconceptions.trap: Once a name is registered it can never be forced to change.
misconceptions.correction: Section 16 allows the Central Government to direct a change for identity, resemblance or inadvertent registration.
It is a company-law rectification power focused on company names under the Act, though trade-mark conflicts may also arise under other law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 16 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the ground (resemblance / inadvertence). II. State the Central Government’s power to direct change. III. Note compliance duty and non-compliance consequences. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Ground for direction; direction status; compliance or default; Registrar action; precise relief.

examTips: Distinguish compulsory rectification from voluntary name change.
Note Central Government and Registrar roles on default.
